rationale:
Single coherent defect: Command's constructor unconditionally called argParser.addFlag('help', ...) even when the command supplied an ArgParser.allowAnything(), and CommandRunner then unconditionally read argResults['help']. Both fail for allow-anything parsers, so any allowAnything-based subcommand was unusable under CommandRunner. The production fix (patches/production-fix.patch, identical to patches/minimized-production.patch) contains exactly two hunks in lib/command_runner.dart that address that pair of unguarded accesses: skip registering the help flag when argParser.allowsAnything, and guard the help lookup with argResults.options.contains('help'). The second hunk is not an unrelated change; it is required because the first hunk removes the 'help' option from such commands. The minimized patch drops the CHANGELOG edit present in patches/original-commit.patch, so nothing documentation-, config-, formatting-, or test-only remains. The trigger is the unmodified upstream test from the same fixing commit ('works as a subcommand in a CommandRunner' in test/allow_anything_test.dart) plus the project-native AllowAnythingCommand fixture in test/test_utils.dart; it exercises only pre-existing public API (CommandRunner, Command, ArgParser.allowAnything(), already covered by the existing 'new ArgParser.allowAnything()' group in the same file at the buggy revision) and does not touch the argParser.allowsAnything / argResults.options members used by the fix, so it introduces no dependency on a fix-introduced API. Machine evidence gates all pass in both strict_original and strict_post_minimization: build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential (reproduced selector matches the declared trigger), trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions), trigger.fixed_clean, and full_suite.fixed_all_green with buggy full-suite failures limited to the declared trigger. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so dart-archive/args#132 duplicates no active registry entry, and it is the sole allowed verified key.

One coherent defect: `Command()` unconditionally called `argParser.addFlag('help', ...)` and `CommandRunner.parse` unconditionally read `argResults['help']`, both of which are invalid for a parser created via the pre-existing `ArgParser.allowAnything()`. The fix in lib/command_runner.dart guards the flag registration with `!argParser.allowsAnything` and guards the lookup with `argResults.options.contains('help')`; both `allowsAnything` and `ArgResults.options` are pre-existing (they are referenced, not introduced, by the patch, which touches only command_runner.dart). The trigger 'works as a subcommand in a CommandRunner' registers an `AllowAnythingCommand` (whose `argParser` is `ArgParser.allowAnything()`, an API already exercised by the pre-existing allow_anything_test.dart group) with a CommandRunner and runs it, hitting exactly the two guarded code paths; it uses no API added by the fix. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test portion of the single fixing commit (test/allow_anything_test.dart plus the test-only fixture in test/test_utils.dart), so it is semantically identical to the reported defect rather than a curator reconstruction. The minimized production patch is byte-identical to production-fix.patch and confined to the two logic hunks in lib/command_runner.dart; the CHANGELOG edit and test/fixture additions from the original commit were correctly excluded, and no formatting, refactor, or feature-extension change remains. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization runs shows all gates green: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (1/1 unique), trigger.buggy_differential with the declared selector failing alone, trigger.fixed_clean across isolated/suite/reversed runs, trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups over 3 repetitions, 32-run matrix), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so no duplicate root cause exists, and dart-archive/args#132 is the sole allowed verified issue key.

risks: Traceability resolves to PR #132 rather than a distinct user-filed issue; issue_urls points at issues/132, which is the same GitHub number as the pull request.
